No ordinary quarry burden or sand-recovery credit is added to this co-product. Keep source producer shares and five freight rows.

Original CN/US/RER native documentation explicitly states dry basis; CH source and native match grass/beet/whey shares and useful-heat/electricity quantities; BR source and native dewatering conventions consume one kg active hydrated ethanol per kg active anhydrous output. Use native CH/US/BR by matching country, native RER for European and otherwise unlocated dewatering, and BR sugarcane/mollasses production for Brazilian, Colombian and RoW sugarcane branches. These complete native proxies replace modern/traditional, annexed/autonomous plant technology and sugar/electricity co-product allocation; they do not reproduce those source production routes. Geographic, feedstock, water, dehydration, energy, allocation, emissions and vintage differences remain explicit. No 1/0.997 multiplier or solvent addition is introduced.

review.reason: Retain both pure-KOH producer shares using complete native KOH per kg active substance and all four original market freight rows. Source explicitly states pure KOH, and its cited original 85.6% production report was subsequently rescaled. Treat native KOH as the documented active-reference screening proxy; do not multiply by 1/0.856, infer concentration from its salt input, or convert K2O-labelled precursor kg as if it were ordinary KCl. Source/native precursor, chlorine/hydrogen allocation, electricity/heat, concentration/drying, upstream transport, geography and vintage differ. Exact reconstruction of source KOH burdens is not claimed.
